events.preview_text: Queue a couple of weeks, then drag today's shop update into place.
events.body:
You can plan a couple of weeks of social posts ahead and still drop in today's news from the shop.

Buffer is scheduling software that lets you queue posts in advance and move them around whenever something changes.

Here's how it works: you add posts to a queue and see them laid out on a calendar across the weeks ahead. When something comes up, drag a post into a new spot, or slot your update into an open one.

So planning ahead doesn't lock you in. Foster Coffee Company, an independent local shop, plans its content two weeks to a month out and still clicks and drags in last-minute changes.

Before you set up a weekly queue, one plain limit: the Free plan holds **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time. The official plan page lays it out so you can see if that's enough to start.
events.postscript: Reordering happens one channel at a time, rather than across all at once.

events.body:
You already plan your own posts, lining them up whenever you get a spare moment.

Getting several ready ahead of time usually means committing to an order. Then a local event or a last-minute special wants to jump the line, and the whole plan needs reshuffling.

Buffer is social media scheduling software for small businesses. You queue your posts, then drag one ahead of the rest to reorder them — so a timely local update slots in without rebuilding the week.

You can try that on Buffer's **free-forever** plan. It lets you connect a few channels and keep up to **10 scheduled posts per channel** queued at a time — no card, nothing to spend.

Foster Coffee Company, an independent shop, plans its posts on Buffer the same way.

Before you set up a week's queue, take a look at what the Free plan covers.

edits.fix: Reframe the opening from a presumed reshuffle struggle toward what the profile supports (they plan their own posts in spare moments) and the brief's real proposition — line a week up ahead and test whether planning ahead fits, free — so the flexibility is a safeguard, not a pain the reader is told they have.

edits.line: Buffer is social media scheduling software for small businesses. You queue your posts, then drag one ahead of the rest to reorder them — so a timely local update slots in without rebuilding the week.
edits.problem: The entire value rests on the drag-to-reorder convenience; readers judged one small feature too thin to justify setting up a new tool and said it doesn't answer a question worth the click.
edits.fix: Connect the queue mechanism to the brief's payoff — building and rearranging a whole week's posts you can try for free before committing — so the feature earns the step rather than standing alone as a reordering trick.

Introduce Buffer through one problem: planning several posts ahead while keeping room for a timely local update. Explain the queue-and-reschedule workflow, use the documented Foster Coffee example only if it earns its space, and state the Free plan scheduling limits plainly. Invite the reader to check the official Free plan before trying a weekly queue. Do not claim Buffer increases organic reach, saves a quantified amount of time, or supports every social channel.
